items.meta_title: VPN Kill Switch: Block Traffic If the VPN Drops | VpnHood!
items.meta_description: The kill switch blocks your internet connection the moment the VPN disconnects, so nothing leaves the device unprotected. Available in VpnHood!
items.title: Kill Switch
items.lead: Automatically blocks the internet connection if the VPN disconnects.
items.shot_alt: The Kill Switch screen in the VpnHood! app
items.platforms: Android, Windows and Linux. On Android it relies on a system setting; on Windows and Linux it is the app's own and can keep the block after you disconnect, and on VpnHood! CONNECT it needs Premium.
items.how_desc: If the tunnel drops, a device would normally fall back to the ordinary connection without telling you. The kill switch blocks traffic instead, so nothing leaves the device unprotected in the gap. In Android settings it is called Block connections without VPN.
items.when_desc: Leave it on whenever an accidental unprotected moment matters more to you than staying online.
items.cost_desc: When the VPN drops you lose connectivity until it is back. Wi-Fi sign-in pages may not load either, so a hotel or airport network can need the switch off for a minute.
items.pair_title: On Android, it needs Always On
items.pair_desc: Android puts the kill switch underneath the always-on VPN setting, so the two are turned on together and work as a pair. Always On brings the tunnel back after a reboot or a change of network; the kill switch holds your traffic until it is actually back. Without it, apps can send a few requests in the seconds before the VPN is up. On Windows and Linux it works without Always On, and the block waits for you to reconnect.
